edition.witness_note: Lake 1912 Loeb copy-text; Lightfoot/Funk middle recension not yet locked as second witness

source_text: [1] Σπουδάσατε οὖν μιᾷ εὐχαριστίᾳ χρῆσθαι: μία γὰρ σὰρξ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ ἓν ποτήριον εἰς ἕνωσιν τοῦ αἵματος αὐτοῦ, ἓν θυσιαστήριον, ὡς εἷς ἐπίσκοπος ἅμα τῷ πρεσβυτερίῳ καὶ διακόνοις τοῖς συνδούλοις μου: ἵνα, ὃ ἐὰν πράσσητε, κατὰ θεὸν πράσσητε.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore be diligent to make use of a single Eucharist, because the flesh of our Lord Jesus Christ is one, and the cup for union with his blood is one, the altar is one, as the bishop is one together with the presbytery and the deacons who are my fellow slaves, in order that whatever you may do, you may do according to God.
pass_b_english: Be eager, then, to use one Eucharist, so that whatever you do, you do it God's way. For there is one flesh of our Lord Jesus Christ, and one cup for union with his blood. There is one altar, just as there is one bishop, with the presbytery and the deacons, my fellow slaves.

choices.why: χράομαι 'use, take part in'; εὐχαριστία here is the rite. 'Use' kept for the verb.

choices.english: one cup for union with his blood
choices.why: εἰς of purpose; the cup unites with his blood.
rejected: to show forth the unity of His blood

choices.why: Short and spoken; 'according to God' sounds foreign in reading text.

anf_compare.notes: Same sense. ANF supplies '[show forth]' and '[the will of]'; we render εἰς ἕνωσιν as purpose without supplements.

notes: One cup and one flesh may recall 1 Corinthians 10:16-17; not cited inline.
Source accent on συνδούλοις kept as supplied.
Repair 2026-10-02 per checker a: ἵνα clause rendered as purpose of 'use one Eucharist' (Greek order: σπουδάσατε… εὐχαριστίᾳ χρῆσθαι… ἵνα… πράσσητε), not a wish.

review.notes: Paragraph 1 matches Philadelphians 4 and Pass A keeps each clause: one Eucharist, one flesh of our Lord Jesus Christ, one cup for union with his blood, one altar, one bishop together with the presbytery and the deacons who are my fellow slaves. Greek 'ἵνα, ὃ ἐὰν πράσσητε, κατὰ θεὸν πράσσητε' is purpose. Pass A has 'in order that whatever you may do, you may do according to God'. Pass B 'And so, whatever you do, may you do it God's way.' makes an inverted wish and drops that purpose link. No false citation is present to fail.
reasons: Pass B contradicts the purpose force of Greek 'ἵνα, ὃ ἐὰν πράσσητε, κατὰ θεὸν πράσσητε' and of Pass A 'in order that whatever you may do, you may do according to God' by writing 'And so, whatever you do, may you do it God's way.'

review.notes: Paragraph 1: Greek source is Ignatius Philadelphians 4 (Lake 1912 Loeb). Pass A gloss: 'Therefore be diligent to make use of a single Eucharist...' correctly translates Σπουδάσατε οὖν μιᾷ εὐχαριστίᾳ χρῆσθαι:..., preserving sense of urgency (Σπουδάσατε), means (χρῆσθαι), and grounds (μία γὰρ σὰρξ... ἓν ποτήριον... ἓν θυσιαστήριον... ὡς εἷς ἐπίσκοπος ἅμα τῷ πρεσβυτερίῳ καὶ διακόνοις). Pass B: 'Be eager, then, to use one Eucharist...' matches Pass A in sense and does not add or contradict; 'Be eager' renders Σπουδάσατε appropriately, 'use one Eucharist' for μιᾷ εὐχαριστίᾳ χρῆσθαι, and the causal/parallel structure (For..., There is..., just as..., And so...) reflects Greek syntax. Scripture note: 1 Corinthians 10:16-17 allusion is correctly noted as not inline, so no citation required. Title 'One Eucharist, One Altar' names the thought. Negation: none present. Agency: subjects preserved (you, bishop, presbytery, deacons). Modality: imperative (Σπουδάσατε) rendered as 'be diligent'/'Be eager'; purpose clauses (εἰς ἕνωσιν, ἵνα) translated with 'for union', 'in order that'. Doctrine: unity of flesh, cup, altar, bishopric upheld. Completeness: all clauses covered; no omission of κατὰ θεόν ('according to God' vs Pass B 'God's way' — both acceptable, Pass B choice justified). No uncertainties.
